And if we love God, and his cause, and his

experience in the religious world for some

does it profit my brethren, though you have

And again. If a brother ora sister be na-

And though mankind has been most shame-
ing, that is no reason why

Brethren beloved, we have unceasing de-

We, know tnis man and his family, his

For the sake of the truth, we will add an-

And this is not all we have been favored with
the privilege of conversing with gentlemen
that have been acquainted with him from
his childhood.and with others and we are glad
to have it to, say that they have invariably had
something good to say about him or in his
favor. And it is unspeakably gratifiing to

in the kingdom and Church of Christ that
he holds, and that the nearer we labor to him
in the vineyard of the Lord the less the op.
position; and to hear his old friends say "we
would like to hear Elder Rigdon preach, and
if he will come and preach for us we will do
our part in bearing his expences."
Brethren, there is no one thing more pleas-
ing, than that a man's character holding
the station that this our beloved brother holds
before God, and his brethren and the world,
is good enough to sustain itself, in spite of
all the opposition that may be against his reli-
